findings.description: Catalog filter strings interpolate raw values (task_type from the request's task_signals, vendor/model/endpoint_kind from refresher and probe rows) without percent-encoding. Both DatabaseClient backends split query_params on '&' (db.py:148 concatenates into the REST URL; db_postgres.py:280 parses parts), and the repo's convention is issue_service._encode_query_value for exactly this reason. An authenticated caller can POST task_signals.task_type='x&limit=0' or 'x&order=...' to alter the posterior query, and any OpenRouter model id containing '&' or '=' corrupts get_entry/upsert. Encode every filter value with the existing helper.
findings.resolution: Wrap every interpolated filter value in the shared encoder (or add one in catalog.py) for list_entries, get_entry, list_candidates, get_decision, and the ledger's date filters.

findings.description: _candidate_payload hardcodes stale_catalog=False and CatalogService.list_candidates drops the row's derived staleness (computed by _with_derived_staleness) when building CandidateInput. The spec requires stale rows to be reported as stale and the Candidate contract carries stale_catalog for that purpose, yet every selection response and persisted decision claims a fresh catalog even when refresh has failed for days.
findings.resolution: Carry row['stale'] through CandidateInput (or a parallel map keyed by vendor/model/endpoint_kind) and populate stale_catalog from it in _candidate_payload.

findings.existing_code:
except RoutingUnavailableError as exc:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc)) from exc
findings.description: Only RoutingUnavailableError maps to 503. A DB outage in catalog.list_candidates or catalog.record_decision (httpx/asyncpg errors) surfaces as an unhandled 500, and record_decision runs after a valid selection so the caller gets a 500 for a decision that was computed but not persisted. The MCP tool select_model_for_task does not map RoutingUnavailableError at all, so the two transports disagree on the no-candidate failure mode. The synchronous seam only tolerates this because it catches everything, but external HTTP/MCP callers do not.
findings.resolution: Catch backend errors in RoutingService.select_model and re-raise as RoutingUnavailableError (or a dedicated storage error mapped to 503), and mirror the same mapping in the MCP tool.

findings.existing_code:
for entry in entries:
            await self._catalog.upsert(entry)
findings.description: The spec says the refresher updates OpenRouter 'pricing and availability', but refresh() only upserts models present in the response. A model removed from OpenRouter keeps available=True forever and stays routable; its refreshed_at also never advances so it becomes 'stale' rather than unavailable, and stale rows are documented as still routable. Also item['id'] raises KeyError on a malformed entry, aborting mid-loop after partial upserts.
findings.resolution: Diff the fetched ids against existing openrouter rows and set_availability(available=False) for the missing ones; skip malformed items instead of aborting the whole refresh.

findings.existing_code:
async def rollup_current_month(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return await self.usage_summary(window="month")
findings.description: The scheduled 'ledger rollup' computes a full-month scan every 5 minutes and discards the dict; nothing is persisted, logged, or exposed, so the watchdog job is a pure read load with no observable effect. Separately, RoutingService.get_usage always returns by_model=[] and exploration_usd_used=0.0 because usage_summary never groups by model or sums rows with exploration=True, even though the ledger rows carry both fields. The UsageAggregate contract advertises both.
findings.resolution: Have usage_summary produce by_model and exploration_usd_used from the rows it already loads, and either persist/log the rollup result or drop the job until it has a consumer.

findings.description: The adaptive branch maps the candidate's catalog vendor onto ResolvedArchetype.provider and drops endpoint_kind. For OpenRouter rows the refresher sets vendor to the model-id prefix (e.g. 'qwen' for 'qwen/qwen3-coder'), so a caller receives provider='qwen', model='qwen/qwen3-coder' with no indication it must dispatch via the OpenRouter endpoint. Existing provider semantics ('codex', 'claude', ...) select CLI/SDK adapters, so an adaptive selection is not actionable by current dispatchers. If adaptive dispatch is out of dg-00 scope, the wrapper should say so; if not, endpoint_kind needs to travel with the result.
findings.resolution: Either add endpoint_kind (and base_url) to ResolvedArchetype or restrict adaptive results to vendors the dispatch layer can route; record the scope decision.

findings.description: OpenAPI declares task_signals.required=[archetype], but SelectModelRequest accepts any dict and _task_type silently routes an archetype-less request as 'unknown/medium-complexity'. Related contract drift in the same module: the 503 raised for no feasible candidate is not declared in v1.yaml; get_usage returns an undeclared top-level estimated_fraction and has no response_model; the 401 responses are declared as RFC 7807 problem documents but the coordinator's verify_api_key returns FastAPI's plain {'detail': ...} body.
findings.resolution: Add a TaskSignals model with required archetype, declare 503 on select_model, add a response_model for usage, and align the 401 declaration with the actual error body.

findings.existing_code:
except Exception as exc:
            await self._catalog.set_availability(
findings.description: The broad except in _probe wraps the success-path set_availability call, so a DB write failure after a healthy probe is reported as the endpoint being down (available=False). Conversely, if set_availability raises inside the except block, the exception escapes probe_all and aborts probing of the remaining endpoints, which the watchdog then records as a single job failure.
findings.resolution: Narrow the try to the HTTP call, and guard the DB writes separately so one endpoint's persistence failure neither mislabels it nor stops the loop.

for row in await self.list_entries(include_unavailable=False):
            post_rows = await self.db.query(
findings.description: list_candidates issues one posteriors query per available catalog row on every select_model call (N+1), and OpenRouterRefresher.upsert does a get_entry plus insert/update per model, so a full refresh of OpenRouter's several hundred models costs 600+ sequential round trips. Both are on the hot or scheduled path and grow linearly with catalog size.
findings.resolution: Fetch posteriors for the task_type in one query and join in memory; batch or upsert-on-conflict in the refresher.

findings.description: _adaptive_task_signals spreads the filtered signals and then unconditionally sets modality='programmatic', overriding any caller-supplied modality (the contract allows 'interactive'). Also, when ROUTING_ADAPTIVE is on but COORDINATION_API_URL is unset, every resolution spawns a thread and logs a warning, which is noisy at phase-resolution frequency; a one-time or rate-limited warning would suffice.
findings.resolution: Default modality only when absent; log the unconfigured-URL case once.

findings.existing_code:
def _per_million(value: Any) -> float | None:
    return None if value is None else float(value) * 1_000_000
findings.description: OpenRouter reports '-1' for dynamically priced models. _per_million converts that to a negative per-Mtok price, which would rank such models as cheaper than zero-cost local endpoints in the cost term.
findings.resolution: Treat negative or non-numeric pricing as None (unknown) so the resolver falls back to the prior/unknown-cost path.

findings.description: _default_routing_jobs runs in WatchdogService.__init__ and parses the three interval env vars with int(); a malformed value raises ValueError and prevents the watchdog from constructing at all, taking the pre-existing stale-agent and vendor-health checks down with it. The same pattern exists in get_usage's float(ROUTING_MONTHLY_CEILING_USD), which turns a typo into a 500 on /routing/usage.
findings.resolution: Parse with a tolerant helper that logs and falls back to the default.

findings.resolution: Audit callers of get_dispatch_configs / the dispatch-configs endpoint and note the new shape in the endpoint's docstring or changelog.

findings.description: test_catalog_read_uses_storage_only_and_derives_staleness asserts external_client.get was never awaited, but external_client is never given to CatalogService, so the 'no external call on the read path' assertion is vacuous and would pass even if list_entries called httpx directly. Likewise test_migrations_catalog only string-matches the SQL; idempotency (second apply preserves schema and data) is asserted by the spec but never executed.
findings.resolution: Patch httpx (or the refresher) in the catalog read test and assert no network call; add a DB-backed migration test that applies 040 twice if the integration suite supports it.
